items.description:

Services (ACS) offerings on September 30, 2028. After this date, the affected
services will no longer be available.  Details
Beginning September 30, 2028, the following ACS services will be retired and will no
longer function: 
 Email 
 SMS 
 Advanced Messaging with WhatsApp 
 Chat 
 Chat for Teams Meeting Interop 
 Rooms 
 Number Management (Direct Offer)Direct Routing 
 Job Router 
 Web UI Library SDK 
 Mobile UI Library SDK Several ACS services will also undergo breaking changes.
These services will continue to function only when used with Microsoft Teams and will require customers to update their applications to the
latest SDKs:

implementation that does not update to the latest SDKs by September 30, 2028, will

and Breaking Change FAQ to learn more. More information  If you have questions, get answers from community experts

items.title: Retirement: Azure Communication Services (ACS) standalone services will be retired on September 30, 2028

items.description: In public preview, Foundry Agent Service adds Foundry Routines, a native trigger primitive for running published agents automatically. Production agents often need to run on a schedule or when a business event occurs, and today that means assembling external glue such as Logic Apps, Azure Functions, webhooks, queues, custom storage, and separate identity and role assignments. The agent is governed in Foundry, but the trigger layer has been customer-owned infrastructure with its own configuration, monitoring, and failure modes. Routines includes recurring schedules, one-shot delayed timers, and event-based triggers through supported connections, keeping triggers, execution, and observability inside the governed Foundry workspace. The preview is intended for evaluation and is not covered by production SLAs. To get started, add a Routine to a published agent in Foundry Agent Service. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Foundry Routines in Foundry Agent Service

items.description: You can now monitor the synchronization status of your logical replication slots in Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server using the new logical_replication_slot_sync_status metric. This Azure Monitor metric shows whether each logical replication slot is synchronized, catching up, or in an unknown state, helping you validate replication health and slot readiness. This feature is especially useful when using logical decoding or change data capture (CDC) tools like Debezium or Kafka. With per-slot visibility and the ability to set up alerts, you can ensure your logical replication setup remains consistent and responsive during planned maintenance, migrations, or system events.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Logical replication slot sync status metric for Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server

items.description: Announcing the addition of enhanced secure authentication in Azure Storage that combines the flexibility of user-delegation shared access signature (SAS) with the user-bound access of Entra ID. User-bound user delegation SAS is now generally available for all regions. User delegation SAS is an existing feature that allows users to create secure SAS tokens that are tied to the delegator, meaning the delegator must verify their identity with Entra to create the token. The resulting token can be traced to the delegator and can only be valid for up to 7 days. This feature is an extension of user delegation (UD) SAS, which is already generally available for Azure Blobs, Azure Files, Azure Tables, and Azure Queues. User-bound user delegation SAS allows users to create a more secure SAS token than account SAS, service SAS, or normal user delegation SAS by restricting the usage of the SAS token to an end user identity. This will help enforce that the user delegated SAS can only be used by intended users.  There is no additional cost to use user-bound user delegation SAS. Pricing is based on standard transaction costs for your storage account type, refer to Azure Storage Pricing for details. This feature is available in all public regions.Learn more: Create a user delegation SAS  Read the announcement blog
items.title: Generally Available: User-bound user delegation SAS for Azure Storage

items.description: We’re happy to announce the public preview of reader endpoint support to simplify connection management when using multiple replicas in Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server. A reader endpoint enables automatic load balancing of read-only connection traffic across multiple replicas. It simplifies application architecture by giving you a single endpoint for read operations, enhancing both scalability and fault tolerance.Azure Database for MySQL supports up to 10 read replicas per primary server. By routing read-only traffic through the reader endpoint, you can efficiently manage connections and optimize performance without needing to handle individual replica endpoints. Available to all Azure customers for non-production use and testing.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Reader Endpoint for Azure Database for MySQL

items.description:
The PostgreSQL skills and MCP plugin turns supported AI coding assistants into context-aware PostgreSQL experts that can both provide guidance and act on a connected database. The bundled plugin combines expert-curated skills for PostgreSQL and Azure Database for PostgreSQL with an MCP server that can inspect your live database context, run queries, apply changes, and support database operations.The plugin uses your schema, PostgreSQL version, extensions, and Azure environment to deliver relevant guidance instead of generic recommendations. It covers scenarios such as query and index tuning, vector search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), JSONB, partitioning, security, Azure provisioning and scaling, high availability and failover, point-in-time restore, AI functions, and knowledge graphs with Apache AGE. It automatically routes between generic PostgreSQL and Azure-specific guidance based on your question and connection context.The plugin is available through supported AI coding assistants, including GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude Code, and Codex CLI. 
Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: PostgreSQL skills and MCP plugin for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: Align Microsoft Marketplace purchases to your business's accounting needs. Purchase order mapping helps allocate your Microsoft invoice, including Marketplace purchases, making it easier to reconcile your organization's cloud and AI spend. Get supplemental invoice views by purchase order and remap spend for up to three months after invoicing, so your teams get the flexibility to adapt as your needs evolve.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Purchase order mapping available in Microsoft Marketplace

items.description: Azure automatically recovers a VM when it loses access to an attached managed disk for an extended period. The VM is shut down and powered back on after disk connectivity is restored, with no customer action required. This remains the default behavior.Now in public preview in select regions, per-disk resiliency provides another option for applications that can tolerate the temporary loss of an individual data disk. When enabled, Azure detaches and takes only the affected disk offline while the VM and its remaining disks continue running. Once disk connectivity is restored, Azure automatically attaches and brings the disk back online.Use per-disk resiliency where a single data disk is not a single point of failure:Production VMs with backup or auxiliary disks, so a secondary disk issue does not interrupt the primary workload.Clustered and shared-disk applications with their own high-availability or failover logic.Containerized workloads with per-pod disks, so one persistent volume can recover without disrupting other pods on the node.Per-disk resiliency is opt-in for each Azure Managed Disk. While a data disk is offline, I/Os to it returns errors, so the application must continue without that disk until access is restored. OS disks continue to use the default VM shut down recovery behavior.Available now in public preview in select regions. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Per-disk resiliency for Azure VMs

items.description:
Azure Front
Door’s Web Application Firewall (WAF) now supports profile and route level WAF
policy associations in public preview. This gives you more flexibility to apply
broad baseline protection across an Azure Front Door profile while using
targeted policies for specific applications, domains, or routes that need
different controls. With this
update, you can associate WAF policies at the profile, domain, or route scope.
For example, you can use a profile level policy for common protections across
all domains in a profile, then apply a route level policy to sensitive paths
such as sign-in, checkout, or API routes. This helps reduce policy duplication
while still allowing more granular security configuration where it's needed. If multiple
WAF policy scopes apply to a request, Azure Front Door uses the most specific
policy: a route level policy takes precedence over a domain level policy, and a
domain level policy takes precedence over a profile level policy. To get
started, create or update an Azure Front Door WAF policy in the Azure portal
and choose the associated scope that matches your deployment needs. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Front Door profile and route level WAF policies

items.description: The Auxiliary table plan in Azure Monitor Logs is a cost-effective option for ingesting and retaining high-volume, verbose logs used for compliance and auditing. Auxiliary Logs is now generally available in the sovereign clouds: Azure Government (Fairfax) and China.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan in Azure Government and China regions

items.description: The Auxiliary table plan in Azure Monitor Logs gives you a cost-effective way to ingest and retain high-volume, verbose logs that you keep for compliance and auditing but rarely query. Two highly requested capabilities are now generally available.Auxiliary now supports a subset of standard Azure tables, in addition to DCR-based custom tables (_CL). You can keep low-value data on its original standard table — retaining its name, schema, and existing queries — instead of building custom pipelines to reshape it.You can also switch existing tables between the Analytics and Auxiliary plans without recreating them. The change applies to the table in place, so you keep history, schema, and integrations, and the switch is fully reversible as your workload evolves.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan support for Azure tables and plan switching

action

items.description:
Microsoft is retiring all versions of HPC Pack. End of
Support is August 27, 2027. HPC Pack is now entering a one-year retirement
period. Microsoft will provide
limited, retirement-only support during this period. The scope of this support
is defined below so customers know what to expect. In scope until End of
Support: • Security/CVE response and necessary security updates. • Guidance from existing documentation and validated
configurations. • Assistance with supported components and documented
functionality. • Case-by-case evaluation of long-term support options where
available. Out of scope: • Non-security fixes or product improvements. • New features, custom code, or design changes. • Validation of new operating systems, hardware,
dependencies, architectures, or integrations. • New product investigation or documentation. • Migration planning, execution, or consulting. • Unsupported configurations. After August 27, 2027, HPC Pack will receive no updates,
fixes, or technical support. Existing deployments will remain operational but
unsupported. Required action Begin assessing and transitioning workloads now. Consider
Azure Batch for managed parallel and HPC scheduling, or another appropriate
Azure service. No alternative guarantees one-to-one feature parity. Engage your
Microsoft account team or Cloud Solution Architect for planning. Share customer needs and transition challenges through this
form: ESU Extend Request.
items.title: Retirement: Microsoft HPC Pack

items.description: Organizations running Windows-based workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) face increasing pressure to modernize as support timelines for older Windows Server versions approach retirement. To help customers prepare, AKS now offers GA support for Windows Server 2025, bringing significant improvements such as Stable ABI, Generation 2 VM default, containerd 2.0, and FIPS enablement by default.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Windows Server 2025 on AKS

items.description: You can now accelerate your containerized workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) using Azure Container Registry (ACR) with Artifact streaming. Artifact streaming will allow you to scale your workloads without having to fully wait for images to be pulled into the clusters.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Artifact Streaming on AKS

items.description: Confidential Virtual Machines (CVM) offer strong security and confidentiality for tenants. CVM for Azure Linux in AKS is now generally available and enables node pools with CVM to target the migration of highly sensitive container workloads to AKS without any code refactoring while benefiting from the features of AKS. You can create new node pools using supported CVM vm sizes with Azure Linux 3. The nodes in a node pool created with CVM use a customized Azure Linux 3 image specially configured for CVM. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Confidential VMs for Azure Linux

items.description:
Azure Copilot Observability Agent, an
AI-powered operational companion in Azure Monitor, is now covering Log Analytics data
in Basic and Auxiliary table plans during interactive analysis
and deep investigations. Teams can move high-volume telemetry - including
container stdout and stderr, audit trails, and node syslog - to
lower-cost table plans while keeping supported data available to the agent
alongside metrics, traces, topology, and Azure resource context. This is especially useful for Kubernetes
operations, where high-volume telemetry such as ContainerLogV2, AKS audit logs, and
control-plane logs can be candidates for the Basic table plan. If eligible tables already use the Basic or Auxiliary plans, no additional user configuration is required.Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Copilot Observability Agent supports Basic and Auxiliary table plans

items.description: Customers can now bring Azure Container Apps environments into Microsoft Defender for Cloud’s Serverless Containers Posture experience, helping security teams extend posture management across more of their container estate from a single workflow. This makes it easier to gain visibility into Container Apps resources and assess risks across areas such as identity, networking, and container or image configuration. With this capability, teams can more consistently evaluate risk across container environments and use attack path analysis to identify potential exposure faster. The result is a more unified security posture, less manual effort, and stronger confidence when securing Container Apps deployments. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Defender for Cloud support for Azure Container Apps (Serverless Containers Posture)

items.description:
Microsoft is retiring Azure Arc-enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager (SCVMM) in September 2029. Customers must plan and transition to alternative solutions.What does this mean for you?If you are using Azure Arc-enabled SCVMM for:Azure services and Azure Arc capabilities such as monitoring, security, governance, updates, and licensing for Extended Security Updates and Pay-as-you-go SQL and WS, we recommend switching to Azure Arc-enabled Servers. VM lifecycle and powercycle operations such as create, start, stop, restart, resize, and self-service VM management, we recommend that you reach out to us through e-mail to arc-vmm-feedback@microsoft.com.What action should you take?Review your current use of Azure Arc-enabled SCVMM.Determine the appropriate migration path: Azure Arc-enabled Servers or if you need help, reach out to Microsoft.Follow the migration guidance to deboard your SCVMM environment from Azure Arc and onboard to your alternative solution.We recommend beginning your transition planning as soon as possible to ensure a smooth migration before retirement. You can also share your feedback or any concerns that you may have during this transition through e-mail to arc-vmm-feedback@microsoft.com.Learn
more.
items.title: Retirement: Azure Arc enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager will be retired September 30, 2029

items.description: Announcing the public preview of Azure Multicloud Interconnect, a managed service that provides private connectivity between Azure and supported cloud providers, with Amazon Web Services (AWS) available as the first supported provider in preview. As organizations increasingly distribute applications, data, AI services, and business-critical workloads across multiple clouds, establishing and operating cloud-to-cloud connectivity can become complex and operationally intensive. Azure Multicloud Interconnect helps simplify this experience by providing a managed connectivity solution that reduces deployment complexity while delivering resilient private, high-performance connectivity between Azure and supported cloud environments.With Azure Multicloud Interconnect, you can deploy a multicloud connection directly from the Azure portal, select your cloud provider, region, and bandwidth, and onboard your environment through a guided experience. Once provisioned, you can connect Azure virtual networks and supported cloud-provider virtual networks through a private cloud-to-cloud connection, helping streamline operations and accelerate multicloud deployments.Key highlights:Managed private connectivity between Azure and supported cloud providersSimplified deployment and onboardingBuilt-in resiliency designed for mission-critical workloadsLearn more: Read the documentation Read the announcement blog
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Multicloud Interconnect

items.description:
Azure Firewall’s auto-learn SNAT routes is now
generally available, automatically learning registered and private destination
prefixes periodically and applying them as No-SNAT ranges to preserve original
source IPs and simplify SNAT management.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Firewall auto-learn SNAT routes

items.description:
Azure Payments HSM v2 is a highly available,
single-tenant Payment HSM service for payment processing, credential issuance,
PIN processing, key management, and authentication data protection. Customers
retain exclusive administrative control of an isolated, single-tenant Payment
HSM cluster while Microsoft manages the underlying infrastructure,
availability, and lifecycle operations. Azure Payments HSM v2 enables customers
to protect sensitive payment assets, maintain key sovereignty, and meet the
stringent security, compliance, audit, performance, and operational
requirements of the Payment Card Industry (PCI). Azure Payment HSM v2 runs in PCI DSS and PCI 3DS
compliant Azure data centers, on security infrastructure certified to FIPS
140-3 Level 3, PCI DSS, PCI 3DS, and PCI PIN (PTS). Because payment HSM
clusters are isolated per customer, customers can deploy the service as a
validated component within their own PCI solution, simplifying ongoing audit
and compliance. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Payments HSM v2

items.description: Azure Ephemeral OS Disk with full caching is now generally available for new virtual machines and Virtual Machine Scale Sets. The capability caches the complete OS image on a VM’s local storage, eliminating remote-storage reads after caching finishes. This delivers consistently fast, low-millisecond OS disk access, up to 10× better I/O performance, and greater resilience during storage interruptions—without slowing VM provisioning because caching runs asynchronously after boot. It is designed for I/O-sensitive, stateless workloads such as AI training and inference, quorum-based databases, real-time analytics, and large-scale services. Full caching uses a VM’s cache, resource, or NVMe disk and reduces available local capacity by twice the OS disk size.It is available across Azure public regions for supported 8-core-and-larger GPU, storage-optimized, memory-optimized, HPC, general-purpose, and compute-optimized VM series. Customers can enable it through Azure CLI, ARM templates, or REST APIs by setting the full-caching option for Ephemeral OS disks.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Ephemeral OS Disk with full caching for VM/VMSS

items.description:
Azure
Virtual Network Manager IP address management is now generally available in
additional regions: US Gov Virginia, US Gov Texas and US Gov Arizona, and China
North 3 and China East 3. In complex
network environments, managing IP addresses effectively is essential. This
feature centralizes IP planning and allocation, allowing users to automatically
assign non-overlapping addresses and prevent conflicts between Azure,
on-premises, and multi-cloud address spaces. It also provides clear insights
into IP usage and allocation across your network resources. Through its
integration with Azure Policy, the feature ensures that virtual networks are
created using the designated IP pool, preventing unintended overlapping
prefixes for both new and existing virtual networks. With cross-region
association, users can manage IP addresses for virtual networks across regions,
allowing customers to plan and govern their full address space globally. Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager IPAM in additional Azure regions

Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server is now
available in Germany West Central, enabling you to connect SQL Server
instances to Azure Arc and take advantage of Azure-based inventory, governance,
security, assessment, and license management capabilities. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server in Germany West Central

Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server is now available in Italy

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server Available in Italy North

items.description:
The Functions on Azure Container Apps (ACA) V1 will be retired on September 29, 2027. After this date, existing Functions on ACA V1 Apps will stop running and no longer process
requests or event-driven triggers. Action required Review your Azure environments and migrate all affected apps
to the Functions on Azure Container Apps(ACA) V2 hosting model before September 29, 2027 to avoid service
disruption. Functions on ACA V2 uses a native Azure Container App configured
with `kind=functionapp`. You can reuse your existing container image; the
standard migration path doesn't require function code changes. Use the Azure
Functions on Azure Container Apps v1 migration assistant to help
migrate your function apps from the V1 to V2 model. To migrate manually 1. Record the V1 app's configuration, including secrets,
identity, networking, and scaling. 2. Create a V2 app with `kind=functionapp` and reapply the
configuration. 3. Test all triggers, shift production traffic, and then
decommission the V1 app. We recommend completing migration and production
validation well before the retirement date. For assistance, contact your Microsoft account team or create
an Azure
support request.  Learn more: Migrate
to Azure Functions v2 on Azure Container Apps Create
an Azure Functions app with auto scaling rules on Azure Container Apps
items.title: Retirement: Functions on Azure Container Apps V1

items.description:
The Azure Developer CLI (azd) Extension Framework is now generally available. The framework enables developers, teams, and partners to extend Azure Developer CLI with custom capabilities that support their preferred application development workflows.With the GA release, organizations can build and distribute extensions that integrate custom tools, automate development and deployment tasks, and provide tailored experiences for cloud application development on Azure. The extension framework helps standardize and simplify developer workflows while allowing teams to incorporate organization-specific processes and tooling.The Azure Developer CLI extension model supports a growing ecosystem of extensions, enabling developers to enhance azd with additional functionality beyond the core CLI experience. This flexibility helps development teams streamline application delivery and adapt azd to their unique requirements.Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Developer CLI (azd) Extension Framework

items.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports agentless migration of on-premises SMB file shares to Azure Files (SMB), in public preview. You can move file data from Windows Server or NAS shares into Azure without deploying, registering, or maintaining a migration agent on-premises.With agentless migration, the Storage Mover service connects directly to your SMB share over your existing private connection (VPN or ExpressRoute) and copies data to the destination Azure file share. Source credentials are stored securely in Azure Key Vault, and Storage Mover's managed identities handle access to both the source secrets and the target share. Configure source and target endpoints, create a job, and start the copy from the Azure portal or Azure CLI. Agentless SMB migration joins Storage Mover's existing agent-based paths for SMB and NFS sources, giving you more flexibility to modernize file storage on your own terms.Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: Agentless migration of on-premises SMB file shares to Azure Files (SMB)

items.description: Playwright Workspaces in Azure App Testing is now generally available in Switzerland North, Japan East, and Australia East.Playwright Workspaces provides fully managed cloud-hosted browsers for running end-to-end Playwright tests at scale, with parallel execution, rich debugging artifacts including traces, videos, and screenshots, and seamless CI/CD integration. Customers can use their existing Playwright test suites and get started in minutes.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Playwright Workspaces in Australia East, Japan East, and Switzerland North

items.description:
Azure
Functions Flex Consumption support for TLS/SSL certificates is now generally
available through a new site-scoped certificate model. Each function app can
hold up to 3 private (.pfx) and 3 public (.cer) certificates uploaded directly,
imported from Azure Key Vault, or issued as free App Service Managed
Certificates to enable custom domains, client-certificate authentication, and
mutual TLS scenarios on Flex Consumption. End-to-end
TLS encryption is also generally available for Flex Consumption and allows traffic
encryption between the platform front ends and the workers that run your
functions. Learn more:  Configure
site-scoped certificates Infrastructure
as code instructions Cross-plan
certificate comparison Configure
end-to-end TLS encryption
items.title: Generally Available: TLS/SSL certificate and end-to-end TLS encryption support for Azure Functions Flex Consumption

items.description: Azure Copilot Troubleshooting Agent is now generally available. Troubleshooting Agent is a unified, built-in Azure Copilot capability that helps customers investigate and resolve operational issues faster. Available through both Azure Copilot and Support + Troubleshooting in the Azure portal, Troubleshooting Agent enables you to move from issue detection to resolution faster by bringing together troubleshooting insights, operational context, and recommended actions in a single experience. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Copilot Troubleshooting Agent

items.description: Updated troubleshooting guidance is now available for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. You can use the expanded documentation to diagnose high CPU, memory, IOPS, temporary file usage, and autovacuum issues, helping you identify root causes and resolve performance problems more efficiently.The updated guidance provides end-to-end investigation workflows for the built-in troubleshooting guides and explains how to correlate Azure Monitor metrics, Query Store statistics, session data, and server logs. You can learn how to configure the required telemetry, identify the query, session, wait event, or configuration behind an issue, and apply targeted mitigations before deciding to scale your server. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: New and improved troubleshooting guides for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters now support PostgreSQL 18, bringing the latest PostgreSQL capabilities to distributed, cloud-scale workloads. You can build new applications or modernize existing ones with the performance, reliability, and developer improvements of PostgreSQL 18—combined with the flexible scaling and operational simplicity of Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters.You can explore PostgreSQL 18 performance improvements, new SQL capabilities, and developer-focused features while scaling distributed workloads across tables, shards, and nodes. Powered by Citus 14.0, elastic clusters bring PostgreSQL 18 capabilities to a fully managed, distributed PostgreSQL experience on Azure.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: PG18 support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters

items.description: In mid-September 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:Configure soft delete for the Azure SQL logical server. When the logical server is deleted, it goes into a soft deleted state and is self-restorable during the configured retention period. Any accidental deletes of the logical server can now be self-recovered within the retention period predictably and consistently, without having to call Microsoft support.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for mid-September 2026

items.description: Automatic Zone Placement for VM Scale Sets (Public Preview) enables Azure to automatically select the best availability zones for your scale set based on SKU availability, capacity, and placement requirements. Instead of manually maintaining zone lists for each region, customers can use a consistent configuration across regions while Azure handles zone selection.Key benefits include:Simplified multi-region deployments with no region-specific zone management.Capacity-aware zone selection to improve deployment and scale-out success.Flexible resiliency controls that let you define zone spread and per-zone capacity limits.Greater allocation flexibility by allowing Azure to use additional eligible zones when needed.Support for both new and existing VM Scale Sets using Uniform or Flexible orchestration modes.By default, Automatic Zone Placement distributes instances evenly across three availability zones, maintains a minimum spread across two zones, limits any single zone to 50% of total instances, and can expand into additional zones if required for scaling. Customers can further customize eligible zones, zone count, balancing behavior, and capacity distribution to meet workload needs.The feature only affects placement of new VM instances and does not rebalance existing VMs. Existing deployments can use Automatic Zone Balance to correct zone imbalances.Automatic Zone Placement is available in public preview through the Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, and REST API. To get started, register the Microsoft.Compute/VmssAutomaticZonePlacement AFEC, use Compute API version March 1, 2026 or later, and configure a VM Scale Set with the Auto zone placement policy.
items.title: Public Preview: Automatic Zone Placement for Virtual Machine Scale Sets

items.description:
Announcing public preview
support for HTTP/3 over QUIC on Azure Application Gateway. HTTP/3 is the next
evolution of HTTP and uses QUIC to improve connection setup time, reduce
latency, and provide better resiliency for modern web applications and APIs. With HTTP/3 support,
Application Gateway can now serve frontend client connections over QUIC,
helping improve performance for latency-sensitive workloads such as web
applications, messaging platforms, mobile experiences, transactions, and APIs.
QUIC reduces connection establishment overhead and supports independent
streams, helping minimize the impact of packet loss and improving
responsiveness over unreliable or high-latency networks. HTTP/3 is configured at the
listener level, allowing you to enable it selectively on Basic listeners.
During public preview, HTTP/3 can be configured by using the Azure portal or
through the REST API. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: HTTP/3 over QUIC support in Azure Application Gateway

items.description: Support for Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service will end on December 10, 2026. Azure Container Linux is the replacement for Azure Linux with OS Guard (preview). Starting on December 10, 2026:Users won’t be able to create new Azure Linux with OS Guard (preview) node pools.AKS won’t produce new node images for affected node pools.Existing node pools won’t receive security patches.On March 10, 2027, AKS will remove the Azure Linux with OS Guard node images. After the images are removed, scaling and remediation operations, including reimage and redeploy operations, will fail for affected node pools. You can use either of the following migration options:Migrate an existing Azure Linux with OS Guard node pool in place by following the Migrate nodes to Azure Container Linux for Azure Kubernetes Service documentation. This operation preforms a standard node image upgrade.Alternatively, create a new Azure Container Linux node pool, migrate and validate workloads, and then delete the Azure Linux with OS Guard node pool. Follow Add Azure Container Linux node pools and remove existing node pools.For other available options, see the AKS node operating system. If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A or AKS GitHub Repository. If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request.
items.title: Retirement: Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service

items.description:
The containerized SAP data connector retired on September 14, 2026 and is unsupported and unmaintained. Existing TLS-compliant agents may continue sending logs through the retired HTTP Data Collector API. Container images will be removed on October 14, 2026, preventing new pulls, installation, redeployment, scaling, replacement, and disaster recovery. Customers must migrate to the supported SAP agentless connector.Learn
more.
items.title: Retirement Update: SAP container images removed October 14, 2026

items.description: Beginning in early October 2026, Windows App will begin using three new wildcard fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) for client-side service traffic to Azure Virtual Desktop. These domains are already included in the cloud-side connectivity requirements. If your organization applies network controls to devices running Windows App, you must allow these endpoints before activation. If the endpoints are not reachable, users may experience sign-in and connection failures.  This is a client-side change for Windows App and is separate from the previous cloud-side domain update. Organizations that have already completed the cloud-side update should still review proxy, firewall, VPN, DNS filtering, and Secure Web Gateway policies that apply to user devices to ensure these endpoints are allowed.This work is part of a wider Microsoft approach to unify domain requirements.Required client-side endpoints*.windows.cloud.microsoft Purpose: General Windows cloud service trafficPort: 443/TCP*.service.windows.cloud.microsoft Purpose: Service traffic which requires optimizationPort: 443/TCP*.windows.static.microsoft Purpose: Static content, installation, and update assetsPort: 443/TCPTimelineWindows App will begin using these endpoints in early October 2026. Who is affected?Organizations that:Use Windows App to connect to Azure Virtual Desktop.Apply firewall, proxy, VPN, DNS filtering, Secure Web Gateway, or similar controls to end-user devices.Potential Impact If these endpoints are unavailable, blocked, or inspected in a way that interrupts the connection, users may experience failures during sign-in, resource discovery, connection, or an active session.Recommended ActionBefore early October 2026:Allow outbound HTTPS traffic on 443/TCP to all three FQDNs in applicable firewall rules, proxy allow lists, VPN configurations, DNS filters, and Secure Web Gateway policies.Review TLS inspection or other traffic interception that could prevent Windows App from reaching Microsoft services. Where permitted by organizational policy, route this traffic directly to Microsoft.If client devices are behind managed network boundary engage the team that manages those controls as early as possible, as approval and change-management processes may require additional lead time.Inform your help desk and update internal network and troubleshoot guide.Learn more:Required FQDNs and endpoints for Azure Virtual DesktopMicrosoft unified cloud.microsoft domain
items.title: Announcing: New Windows App client-side endpoints for Azure Virtual Desktop

items.description: Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes is now in public preview. It is a new deployment option for Azure Red Hat OpenShift that runs the OpenShift control plane as a fully managed service, separate from the worker nodes that run customer applications. Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes accelerates application modernization by providing a fully managed OpenShift platform operated by Microsoft and Red Hat SREs, allowing teams to focus on building applications instead of managing infrastructure. Organizations can modernize at their own pace and run virtual machines, containers, and cloud-native applications on a single AI-ready platform.This deployment model enables developers to move faster. Clusters provision in minutes, and development and test environments can scale down during idle periods and scale back up when needed. This helps teams to accelerate experimentation, shorten testing cycles, and bring applications to production more quickly while optimizing infrastructure spend. Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes simplifies operations across growing multi-cluster environments by separating control plane and worker node lifecycles, giving organizations greater flexibility over application upgrades. Teams can scale across regions and environments, customize networking, and maintain operational consistency while Microsoft and Red Hat manage the underlying platform. Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes strengthens security through managed identity and workload identity, using short-lived, automatically rotated tokens instead of stored credentials. Organizations can integrate with their existing identity providers and enhance compliance with default etcd encryption and bring-your-own- keys to meet data residency, sovereignty, and regulatory requirements. Public preview is available in UK South, Canada Central, Australia East, Switzerland North, Brazil South, Central India, East US 2, and West Europe. To get started, create a new Azure Red Hat OpenShift cluster with hosted control planes through the Azure CLI, REST API, or Bicep. Azure Red Hat OpenShift with standard architecture remains fully supported and actively developed.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes

items.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK). You can encrypt your data using keys stored in an Azure Key Vault or Azure Managed HSM that resides in a different Microsoft Entra tenant than your PostgreSQL server. This update is ideal for SaaS providers and ISVs that need to keep database operations and key ownership in separate tenants. With cross-tenant CMK, you can keep full control of your encryption keys while applications and databases run in a service provider's tenant. This separation helps you meet security and compliance requirements by keeping key management independent from service operations, while allowing you to manage key rotation and revocation on your terms. Learn more

You can now select Azure SQL Database, including Hyperscale, as a migration target directly from the database migration experience in Azure Arc. The workflow brings Azure Database Migration Service and Self-hosted Integration Runtime setup into the guided portal journey, allowing you to assess your SQL Server estate, choose your target, configure
your migration and monitor progress without leaving Arc.Until now, your path from assessment to migration required stepping outside Arc, learning a separate service, configuring a runtime, and moving between multiple tools. This additional effort slowed modernization projects. With this release, the databases Arc already identified as migration-ready become databases you can act on immediately, in the same place you assessed them.You get the same migration dashboard, monitoring experience, and guided workflow already used for other Azure SQL destinations, so choosing Hyperscale does not require learning a new migration methodology. Runtime setup is guided and completed only once, with in-portal instructions that walk you through the process.Learn more.

items.description: Vector search and vector indexes are now generally available in Azure SQL Database. Using the CREATE VECTOR INDEX and VECTOR_SEARCH T-SQL capabilities, you can perform efficient approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searches for AI scenarios such as semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), recommendation systems, and image search. Built on the DiskANN algorithm, vector indexes enable efficient vector similarity search over large datasets while allowing you to combine vector search with relational queries and filtering directly in Azure SQL Database. By bringing AI retrieval directly into Azure SQL Database, you can build AI-powered applications on your enterprise data without requiring a separate vector database, simplifying application architecture while leveraging the reliability, security, and governance capabilities of Azure SQL Database. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Vector search and vector indexes in Azure SQL

items.description: Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams is now generally available. An agent only delivers value once it reaches the people who need it, and Foundry developers previously had no native path to make their agents operational across Microsoft 365, requiring separate deployment pipelines, bot registrations, and app manifests. With this release you publish an agent directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams, where it becomes discoverable to end users in the surfaces where they already work. Published agents remain governed through the same Microsoft Entra and Agent 365 controls IT uses for the rest of the organization, giving admins centralized visibility over their agent fleet from day one, so distribution does not mean giving up governance. To get started, publish your Foundry agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams from the Foundry portal. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams

items.description: In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now lets customers govern the outbound connections a hosted agent can make. Customers author ordered rules matched on destination host, including FQDN with wildcards such as *.contoso.com, with actions to allow, deny, transform outbound request headers, or rewrite the destination. Rules live in the agent's Responsible AI policy and are enforced inside the Foundry-managed agent sandbox before traffic leaves the runtime, so no separate network appliance is required for basic allow-listing. Two enforcement modes are supported: audit, which logs would-deny decisions without blocking, and enforce, which blocks denied traffic, letting teams observe real traffic before switching on enforcement. Every egress decision is emitted to Application Insights for audit. The preview is intended for evaluation and is not covered by production SLAs. To get started, configure egress controls under Guardrails in the Foundry portal. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Network egress controls for hosted agents in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: Microsoft Foundry now exposes enable and disable actions for Foundry agent objects within the Agent 365 governance surface in Microsoft Admin Center, generally available. Administrators can control whether a Foundry agent is available for use across their organization using the same elevation pattern applied to comparable agent application actions, without requiring developer intervention. This fills a core governance gap by bringing Foundry agents into the Admin Center alongside other agent types, so IT and governance teams manage the full agent estate consistently and can meet compliance and security requirements around which agents are active. Broader Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra governance operations such as block, unblock, delete, restore, and owner reassignment continue to expand. To get started, open Microsoft Admin Center and use the Agent 365 governance controls. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Enable and disable controls for Microsoft Foundry agents in Agent 365

items.description: Now you can use ALDO to extend SQL Server support to environments that can’t maintain continuous connectivity to Azure. ALDO is designed for operations in highly regulated, secure, remote, or air-gapped environments, where internet connectivity is restricted or unavailable. SQL Server workloads continue to run entirely on Azure Local infrastructure while maintaining operational independence from cloud connectivity. In addition to traditional database workloads, you can use ALDO to support local AI and intelligent application scenarios in disconnected environments. By keeping data, AI models, and SQL Server workloads within the same secure infrastructure boundary, you can build and run AI-powered solutions without requiring cloud connectivity. This is particularly valuable for defense, government, manufacturing, energy, and remote-edge deployments where data sovereignty, security, and operational continuity are critical requirements. Learn more.

In addition to traditional database workloads, you can use SQL Server on Azure Local to provide a foundation for AI-powered applications and intelligent data solutions. This approach helps you bring AI closer to the data, reducing data movement while supporting governance and compliance requirements. Learn more.

Rather than deploying an operating a complete Kubernetes cluster with a local control plane, Flex Nodes for AKS are designed for connected environments where only the worker nodes run at the edge or on customer infrastructure. items.description: Instant Access for application-consistent restore points on virtual machines (that have Premium v2 or Ultra disks as data disks) is now generally available. With Instant Access, you can begin restoring a disk from a restore point as soon as the snapshot is created, instead of waiting for the background data replication to complete fully. That shortens your recovery time objective when you are bringing a VM back online.What's new at general availabilityThis release introduces “instantAccessState”, a consolidated read-only property on the restore point itself. During preview, customer had to inspect “snapshotAccessState” on each individual disk restore point and work out for themselves whether the restore point as a whole was usable. Now the customer can read one property at the restore point level and decide in a single step whether they can restore, copy, or download it, which removes per-disk polling logic from recovery automation and makes restore decision much simpler.How to use itSet instantAccess to true on the restore point collection to enable Instant Access for every restore point in it and optionally set instantAccessDurationMinutes on the restore point to control how long Instant Access stays active (60–300 minutes; the default is 300). Before you trigger a restore, read instantAccessState on the restore point and decide to restore based on its value rather than aggregating per-disk states yourself. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Instant Access for VM restore points
